summary: Siskiyou NF lookout in Curry County: a 1930s gable-roofed L-4 cab, staffed into the 1940s, gone by 1964. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Gable-roofed L-4 cab, built about 1933 (register and firelookout.com); the 1939 history calls the 1930 cabin R1 type
facts.status_note: Cab abandoned by the 1940s and gone by 1964 per the register; firelookout.com gives 1933 to 1964

staffing.status: staffed in 1914, 1933 and 1941 per the records quoted on the Forest Lookouts page

events.note: Register dates a frame shake cabin on a 15-ft platform tower; the 1914 Forest Lookouts accounts show a tent in use instead

Gable-roofed L-4 cab built about 1933 per the register and firelookout.com; conflicts with the 1930 date

Gone by 1964 per the register; firelookout.com gives 1964 as the end date

corrections.proposed: L-4 (gable-roofed cab, per the register and firelookout.com); the 1939 history calls the 1930 cabin R1 type
corrections.why: D-6 appears in the 1926 Siskiyou Bulletin only for the standard building on Mt. Emily, not for Packsaddle. The register and firelookout.com both describe an L-4 cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates a 1913 frame shake cabin on a 15-ft platform tower. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a tent in use in 1914 and a shake-type house planned in 1915 and built by the 1939 history's account. The story reports both and does not choose.

The 1939 forest history dates a new R1-type cabin to 1930, and the 1930 Siskiyou Bulletin says the new house was about complete. The register and firelookout.com date an L-4 cab to about 1933. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today. The register's coordinates (42.02758, -124.02256) differ from the second database in the brief (42.03067, -124.00786); that database was not checked, so the coordinates are unresolved. The brief's D-6 design looks wrong (see corrections). The 1913 vs 1914-1915 start and the 1930 vs 1933 cab date are both disputed and both are reported. The 1939 history and Siskiyou Bulletin quotes come through the Forest Lookouts transcription, not the originals.
